Bootstrap intervals for gauge R&R statistics

Source: R/grr.R
msa_boot.Rd

Parametric bootstrap of the fitted mixed model (lme4::bootMer()): the model is simulated nsim times, refitted and the gauge R&R statistics recomputed. Percentile intervals are returned. With few prompt or model levels the intervals are wide and asymmetric, which is the honest answer; msa_plan() shows how study size changes this.

Usage

msa_boot(fit, nsim = 200, level = 0.95, seed = NULL, ...)

Arguments

fit

An msa_fit of type numeric or binary.

nsim

Number of bootstrap samples.

level

Confidence level.

seed

Optional seed.

...

Passed to lme4::bootMer(), e.g. parallel = "multicore".

Value

A data.frame with the point estimate and interval for each statistic, plus the bootstrap replicates as attribute boot.

Details

Available for numeric and binary outcomes (lme4 models). For ordinal outcomes fitted with ordinal::clmm a parametric bootstrap is not yet implemented; as a pragmatic alternative, score the categories numerically and fit type = "numeric", or treat the top category as a binary outcome.

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- msa_fit(ic50_demo, type = "numeric")
msa_boot(fit, nsim = 50, seed = 1)
#> Parametric bootstrap, 50 replicates, 95 % percentile intervals
#>                      statistic estimate lower upper
#>              grr_pct_study_var    20.51 13.82 32.02
#>           grr_pct_contribution     4.21  1.91 10.25
#>    repeatability_pct_study_var    11.78 10.17 15.78
#>  reproducibility_pct_study_var    16.79  8.89 28.96
#>                            ndc     6.00  4.00 10.00
#>                      icc_items     0.96  0.90  0.98
# }
